title: Erdős Problem #1112: a complete, machine-checked resolution (paper, Lean 4 development, and certificate data)
description:
The complete research artifact accompanying the resolution of Erdős Problem #1112: for every k ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ d1 < d2, the ratio rk(d1,d2) exists if and only if d2 ≥ k+1, with the explicit bound rk ≤ 192d2 on the existence side and strong non-existence below the threshold.

This archive contains:

  • The paper (paper/friendly/), written from first principles: every prerequisite is built in, the idea of each construction is separated from the estimates that pay for it, and the finite certificate layer is printed in full. A compressed presentation of the same results, in the conventional idiom, is included as paper/erdos1112.pdf.
  • The Lean 4 formalization (lean/): the full dichotomy, sorry-free, depending only on the three standard foundational axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), with no native_decide — so every finite check is discharged by the trusted kernel.
  • The certificate data (paper/data/) and two independent Python verification harnesses (paper/scripts/), sharing no code.
  • The documented prior-art search (paper/novelty-search.md) for the bounded subset-sum covering lemma.

This DOI resolves to the archived snapshot cited in the paper's data-availability section.
